chunks: He said: Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn Umar al-Ji'abi reported to me from Abu Abdillah Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Ja'far al-Hasani, who reported from Isa ibn Mihran, from Yunus, from Abdullah ibn Muhammad ibn Sulaiman al-Hashimi, from his father, from his grandfather, from Zainab bint Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon them both) who said:

When the opinion of Abu Bakr became unanimous about depriving Fatimah (peace be upon her) of Fadak and al-Awali, and she lost all hope about his reconsideration, she came to her father's grave - the Messenger of God, may God bless him and his family - threw herself upon it and complained to him about the way the people had treated her. She wept until the earth on his grave became wet with her tears, and she mourned him. Then she said at the end of her lamentation:

"There have been after you news and turmoil; had you witnessed them, the calamities would not have multiplied. We have missed you as the parched land misses the rainfall; your people are in total disarray, so witness them, for they have gone astray. Jibreel used to comfort us with the verses, but now that you are hidden from us, all goodness is concealed. You were a full moon and a light that illuminated; upon you the Books were revealed from the Lord of Might. Men have attacked us harshly and we have been humiliated after the Prophet, and all good has been usurped. The perpetrator of injustice to our family will know on the Day of Resurrection where he will end up. We have endured what no one from creation has endured, neither non-Arab nor Arab. So we shall continue weeping for you as long as we live, and as long as we have eyes that pour forth flowing tears."

key_terms.العوالي: Al-Awali - elevated districts near Medina, another property claimed by Fatimah
key_terms.فدك: Fadak - a fertile land near Medina that the Prophet gifted to Fatimah, later confiscated by the first caliph
key_terms.مغتصب: Mughtasab - usurped, seized by force without right
key_terms.هنبثة: Hanbatha - turmoil, confusion, a rare classical Arabic word for upheaval

ai.seo_question: What did Fatimah al-Zahra (AS) say at the grave of the Prophet Muhammad (SAWW) about Fadak?
ai.summary: This narration, reported through Zainab bint Ali (AS), recounts the moment when Fatimah al-Zahra (AS), daughter of the Prophet Muhammad (SAWW), visited her father's grave after being denied the property of Fadak and al-Awali by Abu Bakr. She wept bitterly and recited a famous elegiac poem lamenting the injustices that befell the Prophet's family after his death. The elegy is one of the most well-known expressions of grief in Shia literature, addressing the Prophet directly about the post-Saqifa turmoil and the usurpation of Ahlulbayt's rights.
